notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes to give you. My first search attempt was blocked because the session had no tool calls left, and nothing came back. Since you asked me to report only what the approved sites actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, I haven't written any verse notes. Commentary from memory, without real URLs, would break both rules.

If you run the request again in a new turn, I'll start with these searches and pages, all on your approved list:

- **Main verse-by-verse sources:**
  - enduringword.com (David Guzik on Psalm 123)
  - the biblehub.com commentary pages for Psalm 123:1–4 (Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Gill, Barnes, Matthew Henry)
  - studylight.org (Gill's Exposition, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*)
  - preceptaustin.org's Psalm 123 page
- **Teachers by tradition:**
  - spurgeon.org, desiringgod.org and gty.org (Baptist)
  - wesley.nnu.edu, for Wesley's notes (Methodist)
  - ligonier.org and thegospelcoalition.org (Reformed)
  - lcms.org and 1517.org (Lutheran)
  - samstorms.org and enduringword.com (Pentecostal and charismatic)
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org translator notes, for example on "contempt," "scorn" and the "hand of the master" image
  - bibleodyssey.org, on the Songs of Ascents as pilgrimage psalms
  - newadvent.org, for Augustine's *Expositions on the Psalms*, Psalm 123 (his numbering is Psalm 122)
  - oca.org, for how this psalm is used in Orthodox worship

After that, I'll write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after every point, and leave out anything the pages don't cover. That includes any tradition differences or popular modern teachings the sources don't actually discuss.
